extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, policymakers, Congressional staff, IP stakeholders, and the public
extracted.subtask_description: Annual performance and accountability reporting of USPTO programs and international IP engagement, including measurable targets and outcomes for training, outreach, worksharing (PPH/PPG), attaché activities, and data releases. Focused on FY2021 metrics and programmatic guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: GIPA training programs conducted
rubrics_metrics.description: In FY 2021, the USPTO conducted 250 training programs through its Global Intellectual Property Academy (GIPA), including programs coproduced with the USPTO’s regional offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs served over 17,800 individuals; quarterly program counts are reported (see Figures 23 and 24). Programs were delivered in-person and virtually and targeted a mix of domestic stakeholders and foreign officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of people trained (GIPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure: number of people, including foreign government officials and U.S. stakeholders, trained on best practices to protect and enforce IP. Fiscal-year target: 5,000; FY2021 actual: 17,841.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure updated in FY2018 to include U.S. stakeholder education. The report provides historical targets and actuals (Table 21) and notes trends and variability in predicting future results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendee composition for GIPA programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 43% of all attendees were representatives of domestic small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), IP practitioners, and IP owners and users; approximately 57% were patent, trademark, and copyright officials; prosecutors; police; customs officials; and policy makers from the United States and 131 other countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composition breakdown is used to characterize reach and target audience mix for GIPA programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distance learning / remote engagement capability
rubrics_metrics.description: GIPA conducted/delivered 250 programs with a distance learning or remote engagement component in FY2021 and maintained capacity for all-remote delivery (pivot begun mid-FY2020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes technological capabilities such as virtual international meetings with simultaneous interpretation, recordings and materials access, and on-demand modules to expand reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-demand content availability and reach
rubrics_metrics.description: GIPA produced on-demand content available in five languages covering six areas of IP protection and enforcement; self-study materials and modules have drawn nearly 200,000 unique views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On-demand materials include recordings of events, training slides, IP toolkits, updated introductory videos (e.g., 'Introduction to Patent Protection'), and micro-learning videos; availability and unique views are tracked as outreach metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public information campaigns (Go for Real / Dupe Detector)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Go for Real anti-counterfeiting campaign educates tweens, teens, caregivers, and educators about counterfeit goods; FY2021 release included the Dupe Detector e-book kit (educational information, activities, online shopping game).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Campaign materials are distributed to local law enforcement for community outreach; effectiveness measured by distribution and usage of kits and materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic government official training
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO provides IP training for U.S. government officials at federal, state, and local levels, including a decades-long partnership with the Department of State’s Foreign Service Institute and programs with the National Association of Attorneys General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs include intermediate and advanced training in all areas of IP and are delivered in-person and virtually; target audiences include federal government officials and state attorneys general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conducting Congressional studies and responding to RFIs
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO conducts studies and issues reports at Congressional request (e.g., report on state infringement; study on effect of section 101 jurisprudence with Federal Register request for information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports summarize findings, may identify instances of infringement, and can include requests for public input (RFI) to inform policy and legislative engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combat the sale of counterfeit goods (policy leadership)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO participates in implementing actions from the DHS report 'Combating Trafficking in Counterfeit and Pirated Goods,' leads efforts assessing secondary trademark infringement liability for platforms, and works to establish a national consumer awareness campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities include assessing administrative/statutory/regulatory actions and promoting private-sector best practices; leadership role in interagency working groups is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH filings and outcomes (worksharing metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cumulative PPH filings and grants are tracked (as of Sept 30, 2021: cumulative total of 74,549 applications with petitions filed under the PPH, with 65,906 patents granted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH is measured as a worksharing mechanism that allows accelerated prosecution across participating offices; cumulative filings and grant counts are used to assess adoption and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global PPH / IP5 PPH adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress toward a global PPH framework (and IP5 PPH) to replace multiple bilateral PPH arrangements with a single, centralized framework to create efficiencies for IP offices and applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption and simplification of worksharing frameworks are evaluated by participation, filings, and the extent to which frameworks reduce applicant burden and office workload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel Patent Grant (PPG) collaboration outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPG collaboration with Mexico’s IMPI (launched Dec 7, 2020) is a form of patent worksharing that facilitates expedited grants of Mexican patents for parties who have USPTO-granted patents for the same invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program design, invitation/eligibility procedures (IMPI-identifies qualifying Mexican applications), and initial phase participation are tracked as program metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent validation arrangement (country-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: patent validation arrangement with Cambodia allowing a holder of a U.S. patent to request issuance of a corresponding Cambodian patent without substantive examination if certain requirements are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such arrangements are assessed based on whether requirements are met and the extent to which they facilitate foreign patent issuance for U.S. rights holders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvements to global industrial design system
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO efforts include leading WIPO discussions on new technological designs (GUIs, icons, typefaces), developing recommended practices for design filing, 3D printing, and remedies for infringement, and organizing forums and APEC programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progress is measured by project milestones, recommended practices produced, and international engagement (e.g., virtual forums).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvements to global trademark system
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress includes expansion of a harmonized pick list of trademark goods/services descriptions, translation of entries, a TM5 project to combat fraudulent solicitations, and projects to exchange operational information among trademark offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metrics include adoption of pick list entries, translations completed, project outputs, and engagement at WIPO and TM5 forums.

rubrics_metrics.name: IP Attaché Program activities and output metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The IP Attaché Program selects IP experts to serve abroad to advocate for improved IP policies and provide training/technical assistance. FY2021 metrics: 13 attachés; assisted 8,993 U.S. stakeholders; conducted 3,909 meetings with foreign officials; 89 training programs for 4,097 participants; 68 public awareness programs for 7,791 participants; submitted 519 weekly activity reports; reported 71 identifiable successes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program improvements tracked include elevating diplomatic rank, deploying attachés to new posts, and enhancing interactions with U.S. stakeholders and rights-holder groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of countries trained by GIPA (reach metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cumulative number of countries trained by GIPA is tracked by quarter and year (Figure 26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geographic reach (number of countries represented) is used to assess international impact and coverage of capacity-building programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance target: prioritized countries progress metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure: percentage of prioritized countries for which IP country teams have made progress on at least three of the four performance criteria. FY targets shown (e.g., FY2021 target 66.0%) and actuals by year are reported (Table 22).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure updated in FY2018 to reflect decrease in number of prioritized countries from four to three; trend analysis and target attainment ('Target met') are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four performance criteria for IP country teams
rubrics_metrics.description: The four criteria used to evaluate country progress: (1) Institutional improvements of intellectual property (IP) office administration for advancing IP rights; (2) Institutional improvements of IP enforcement entities; (3) Improvements in IP laws and regulations; (4) Establishment of government–to–government cooperative mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progress on at least three of these four criteria is the basis for the prioritized-countries performance measure; Table 22 reports percentages and targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and quality of IP data (OCE datasets / AIPD)
rubrics_metrics.description: OCE released six datasets covering a broad scope of IP-related information; OCE published academic work including the AIPD dataset identifying patents with AI technology components and providing documentation and the patent documents used to train the ML model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Datasets are made publicly available on the USPTO website and accompanied by technical working papers to document contents and aid reuse; dataset releases are tracked as outputs supporting policy and research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement in international policy and trade fora
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO provides technical advice and representation in international negotiations and fora (WIPO, USMCA IPR Committee, USTR Special 301, Notorious Markets List, WTO trade policy reviews, negotiations such as U.S.-UK and U.S.-Kenya, ICANN WHOIS issues, and others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effectiveness measured by participation in committee meetings, inputs to trade negotiations, submissions/comments, and monitoring implementation of agreements (e.g., USMCA, Phase One Agreement).
